pomodoro-mistakes.alt: A round timer icon beside a checklist of one tick and two crosses, above a striped bar snapped apart along a jagged tear
pomodoro-mistakes.caption: Most Pomodoro problems come down to a handful of repeatable mistakes, and each one has a specific, fixable cause.

pomodoro-schedules.alt: A row of connected rounded blocks divided by short dashed breaks, extending from a small round fruit-shaped icon
pomodoro-schedules.caption: A Pomodoro schedule is a repeating pattern of work blocks and short breaks, and the ratio can be adjusted through the day.

pomodoro-sound-alerts.alt: A desktop computer and a mug of coffee beside a bell icon with sound waves radiating outward
pomodoro-sound-alerts.caption: The right alert sound signals the end of a session clearly, without the jolt of stress a harsh alarm can cause.

pomodoro-technique.alt: Person working at a laptop beside an oversized kitchen timer, with four stacked blocks marking finished work sessions
pomodoro-technique.caption: Each block is one pomodoro: a fixed stretch of focus followed by a short break, repeated until the task is done.

pomodoro-vs-52-17.alt: A small control icon branching into two toggle-switch shapes of different lengths, each set on a rounded base
pomodoro-vs-52-17.caption: The 52/17 method runs on two separate timers, one for the work stretch and a shorter one for the break that follows.

pomodoro-vs-flowtime.alt: A segmented circular dial on one side and a free-flowing wavy ribbon on the other, divided by a vertical line
pomodoro-vs-flowtime.caption: Pomodoro locks focus into fixed, equal segments, while flowtime lets a working stretch run until concentration naturally breaks.

pomodoro-vs-time-blocking.alt: Rows of unequal schedule bars on one side and a bordered oval with radiating lines on the other, split by a line
pomodoro-vs-time-blocking.caption: Pomodoro repeats identical timed blocks, while time blocking carves the day into custom-sized chunks fitted to each task.

presentation-timer.alt: A speaker gesturing beside a lectern and a screen showing coloured squares and bars, with a segmented dial behind them
presentation-timer.caption: Keeping a visible timer running while presenting helps a speaker pace each slide without losing the room or overrunning.

pressure-cooker-timer.alt: A pressure cooker releasing steam from its lid, positioned beside a round dial with an orange indicator segment
pressure-cooker-timer.caption: A pressure cooker holds steam well past boiling point, so cook times run far shorter than on the stovetop or in the oven.

productivity-timer-for-adhd.alt: Overlapping coloured timer panels stacked at angles above a pedestal, with a segmented gauge visible below
productivity-timer-for-adhd.caption: ADHD brains often respond better to several visible timer formats at once rather than a single standard countdown.

project-sprint-timer.alt: Three columns of small task cards pointed by an arrow toward a circular segmented gauge
project-sprint-timer.caption: A sprint timer sets a fixed window around a batch of tasks, turning an open-ended backlog into a bounded push.

rabbit-lifespan.alt: A rabbit sitting beside a clump of grass, with a circular clock face of tick marks arched behind it like a halo
rabbit-lifespan.caption: How long a pet rabbit lives depends heavily on breed, diet, neutering status and whether it lives indoors.

reading-session-timer.alt: An empty chair beside a small table with an open book, a bookmark ribbon and a mug, under a round wall clock
reading-session-timer.caption: How long a reading session should run depends on the material, with denser non-fiction needing shorter, more frequent sittings.

rest-timer-strength-training.alt: A person resting on a weight bench with their head in their hand, beside a large clock face and a dumbbell on the floor
rest-timer-strength-training.caption: Rest between sets needs to match the goal, running to several minutes for maximal strength and far less for muscular endurance.

rest-timers-strength.alt: A loaded barbell on a rack beside a water bottle, next to a circle divided into four coloured quadrants
rest-timers-strength.caption: The right rest period between sets scales with the goal, longest for strength and shortest for muscular endurance.

rice-cooking-timer.alt: An open rice cooker with fluffy cooked rice and rising steam, positioned in front of a round segmented clock face
rice-cooking-timer.caption: Cooking time and water ratio both shift by rice variety, so a single timer setting rarely suits every type of rice.

rice-timer.alt: A bowl of steaming cooked rice beside a glass of hot water and a round orange alarm clock icon
rice-timer.caption: Getting rice right is mostly a matter of timing the cook and the rest period accurately rather than guesswork.

running-interval-timer.alt: A runner sprinting up a striped diagonal track toward a large circular target icon
running-interval-timer.caption: Interval running alternates hard, timed efforts with recovery, and a timer keeps each segment honest rather than judged by feel.

science.alt: A ringed planet and a small rocket near a large circular dial with a wedge-shaped beam pointing into its centre
science.caption: Space and science topics range from orbital mechanics to the physics that timers rely on to measure a second at all.

second-timers.alt: A large stopwatch beside three smaller square icons, each showing a miniature stopwatch face in a different colour
second-timers.caption: Second-level timers suit tasks measured in short, precise bursts rather than the minutes a typical countdown covers.

sleep-meditation-timer.alt: A person sleeping on their side under a blanket, with small sparkles above them and an hourglass on a bedside table
sleep-meditation-timer.caption: Around twenty minutes of guided meditation before bed is the session length most commonly recommended for winding down.

sleep-meditation-timers.alt: A seated meditating figure beside an hourglass and a bed with striped bedding, under a crescent moon
sleep-meditation-timers.caption: Meditation and sleep timers serve different purposes, one guiding a wind-down session and the other easing the drift into sleep.

sleep-timer.alt: A bed with a small glowing screen on it beneath a crescent moon, beside a round dial device on a bedside table
sleep-timer.caption: A sleep timer switches audio off automatically after a set period, so a device does not keep playing through the night.

slow-cooker-timing-guide.alt: A slow cooker with visible food chunks inside, releasing steam, beside a partly visible round dial
slow-cooker-timing-guide.caption: Low and high settings on a slow cooker cook at different rates, so converting a recipe means adjusting time, not just heat.

sourdough-proofing-timer.alt: A domed ball of dough with visible surface bubbles rising from a ridged proofing basket, beside a small round timer
sourdough-proofing-timer.caption: Sourdough proofing time swings with starter strength and room temperature, so a fixed number of minutes rarely applies twice.

sous-vide-timer.alt: A cut of meat sealed in a bag submerged in a water bath with rising bubbles, next to an immersion circulator and a stopwatch
sous-vide-timer.caption: Sous vide holds food at one precise temperature for an extended time, so the timer matters as much as the setting itself.

spaced-repetition-timer.alt: Five card icons connected by a rising and falling wavy line, ending at a stopwatch
spaced-repetition-timer.caption: Spaced repetition schedules each review at a slightly longer interval than the last, timed to catch memory just before it fades.

speed-reading-timer.alt: An open book with striped text lines and a sweeping arrow beside a round clock face with dotted markers
speed-reading-timer.caption: Speed reading is built through timed, deliberate practice drills rather than simply reading faster by habit.

sports.alt: A ring surrounded by a rugby ball, a basketball, a stack of hockey pucks and a tennis ball
sports.caption: Game length varies enormously by sport, from a fixed running clock to stoppages that can stretch a match well past regulation.

sprint-timer.alt: A sprinter bursting from starting blocks with motion trails, running toward a large stopwatch
sprint-timer.caption: A sprint timer applies the same all-out urgency to a work task that a stopwatch brings to the blocks at the start of a race.

steak-timer.alt: A steak in a frying pan with a thermometer probe inserted, beside a dial gauge and three steak cross-sections
steak-timer.caption: Steak doneness is really a target internal temperature, and a timer alone only gets close without checking that directly.

stopwatch.alt: A classic stopwatch face with a single hand and a two-toned outer ring, split between purple and cyan
stopwatch.caption: A stopwatch counts time running forward from zero, the opposite of a countdown timer that runs down to it.

stopwatch-clock-tools.alt: A row of overlapping timepiece icons: a stopwatch, an alarm clock, an hourglass and a plain wall clock
stopwatch-clock-tools.caption: Stopwatches, countdown clocks and hourglasses all measure time but suit different jobs, from lap splits to visual countdowns.

stretching-timer.alt: A person in a seated forward stretch with a loop strap around one foot, beneath a round wall clock
stretching-timer.caption: Static stretches need to be held for a set duration to improve flexibility, which is exactly what a stretching timer paces.

stretching-timer-guide.alt: A person stretching forward on a mat toward one foot, beside a large quadrant-marked clock face and a rolled foam roller
stretching-timer-guide.caption: Each static stretch works best held for around thirty seconds and repeated several times per muscle after a short warm-up.

study-timer.alt: Person seated at a desk writing beside a stack of books and a desk lamp, with a segmented clock face behind them
study-timer.caption: A dedicated study timer keeps a session running in the background while you work through your notes and reading.

study-timer-for-adhd.alt: A small alarm clock, a cup holding two crossed pencils, a stack of loose papers, and an open book arranged as study items
study-timer-for-adhd.caption: Visual and tactile cues like these can help ADHD learners track time and stay anchored to a study session.

study-timer-methods.alt: Three icons: a segmented progress bar, five rounded blocks in a row, and a circular arrow cycle around a small clock
study-timer-methods.caption: Different study timer methods split focus and rest in different ratios, from short Pomodoro sprints to longer ultradian blocks.

study-work-timers.alt: A laptop with tinted cards behind its screen, a dial gauge, a cup of coffee, and a row of coloured blocks lined up below
study-work-timers.caption: Whether you are studying or working, the right timer keeps focused blocks and breaks visible at a glance.

tabata-timer.alt: A person in a lunging, explosive stance beside a large wheel divided into eight alternating segments
tabata-timer.caption: A Tabata timer cycles through short bursts of all-out effort and brief rest, tracked round by round on the dial.

tabata-timer-guide.alt: A person in a kneeling plank exercise position beside a wheel split into eight alternating blue and amber segments
tabata-timer-guide.caption: Tabata's original protocol packs eight rounds of 20 seconds of work and 10 seconds of rest into just four minutes.

tabata-timer-variations.alt: A person crouched low with clenched fists and motion lines around them, next to a partially filled ring gauge
tabata-timer-variations.caption: Beyond the classic 20:10 ratio, Tabata-style timers can be adjusted for different work-to-rest ratios and intensity levels.

tea-coffee-timers.alt: A kettle and a French press with steam rising from both, and a small stopwatch set between them
tea-coffee-timers.caption: Steeping tea and blooming coffee both depend on precise timing, from a couple of minutes for tea to a short bloom before coffee brews.

tea-timer.alt: A kettle pouring water into a glass containing a tea bag, beside a round timer dial split into two colours
tea-timer.caption: A tea timer counts down the steep so the tea bag comes out at exactly the right moment.

tech.alt: A smartphone, a laptop, a pair of wireless earbuds, a smartwatch, and a circular progress ring arranged together
tech.caption: Timers work across every device, from a phone in your pocket to a laptop browser tab or a smartwatch on your wrist.

time-blocking-timer.alt: A weekly grid with some columns filled by stacks of coloured blocks and others left empty, beside a small clock
time-blocking-timer.caption: Time blocking assigns each task a fixed slot on the calendar, leaving some blocks committed and others deliberately free.

timer-accuracy.alt: A browser window containing a clock face, with a magnifying glass held over part of the dial
timer-accuracy.caption: Browser timers stay accurate to within a small margin per minute while the tab is active, but can drift once it moves to the background.

timer-accuracy-comparison.alt: A browser window, a phone screen, and a physical alarm clock, each displaying the same partly filled progress dial
timer-accuracy-comparison.caption: Browser, app and hardware timers all display time the same way, but their underlying accuracy can vary in ways that matter.

timer-for-kids.alt: A child sitting on the floor brushing their teeth beside a large wall clock, with a bin of toys and a ball nearby
timer-for-kids.caption: A visible timer can turn routine tasks like brushing teeth into something a child can watch counting down.

timer-for-remote-workers.alt: A laptop showing a grid of coloured tiles on a desk with a mug and a small potted plant, beside the edge of a large dial
timer-for-remote-workers.caption: Remote workers without office cues can use a visible timer to mark the boundaries between focused work and breaks.

timer-offline-after-load.alt: A browser window containing a dial gauge, connected by a dashed line to a cloud icon
timer-offline-after-load.caption: Once the page has loaded, the countdown runs entirely in the browser and no longer needs that connection to the cloud.

travel.alt: A suitcase, a passport, an airplane, a globe and a clock linked together by a dotted circular path
travel.caption: Travel timers help track flights, layovers, and time zone changes as you move between places.

turkey-timer.alt: A whole roast turkey in a dish inside an open cabinet, with a round timer and a basting brush beside it
turkey-timer.caption: A turkey timer counts down the roasting time so the bird comes out of the oven fully cooked and ready to rest.

turtle-lifespan.alt: A turtle walking across a mound of ground, with a clock face rising behind its shell like a sun
turtle-lifespan.caption: Turtles are known for long lifespans, though how long one actually lives depends heavily on the species and its care.

ultradian-rhythm-timer.alt: A person working at a laptop beside a large hourglass, with a wavy ribbon path running behind them
ultradian-rhythm-timer.caption: The ultradian rhythm theory suggests focus naturally rises and falls in cycles of roughly ninety minutes.

use-cases.alt: Five circled icons arranged around a central clock dial: a cooking pot, a dumbbell, a crescent moon, a plant, and an open book
use-cases.caption: The same timer works for cooking, exercise, sleep, growth, and reading, wherever a countdown is useful.

visualization-meditation-timer.alt: A person seated cross-legged with eyes closed, a cloud containing mountain shapes above their head, and an hourglass beside them
visualization-meditation-timer.caption: Visualization meditation uses mental imagery, like picturing a landscape, held for a set stretch of time marked by the timer.

walking-meditation-timer.alt: A simple figure walking along a curved path between plants, with an hourglass standing beside the path
walking-meditation-timer.caption: Walking meditation is paced slower than an ordinary walk and is typically timed over a session of several minutes.

warm-up-timer-guide.alt: A person in a running pose beside a large dial gauge, with a small rising wavy line graph beneath them
warm-up-timer-guide.caption: A short warm-up gradually raises the body's readiness before a workout, tracked here as rising activity on the timer.

white-noise-timer.alt: A bedroom with a bed and picture frames, a small speaker on a nightstand, and a wavy sound-wave band crossing the room
white-noise-timer.caption: A white noise timer lets the sound run for a set stretch of sleep or focus time before switching off on its own.

work-break-ratio-timer.alt: A balance scale holding two blocks of different sizes, resting on a stand shaped like a segmented clock dial
work-break-ratio-timer.caption: Choosing a work-break ratio is about balancing enough focused time against enough recovery to sustain it.

workout-timers.alt: A dumbbell, a coiled ring, a kettlebell, and a jump rope arranged together with a blank rounded panel
workout-timers.caption: From strength sets to skipping rounds, workout timers keep every exercise on a consistent schedule.

world-clock.alt: A globe encircled by orbiting rings holding five clock faces, each showing a different time
world-clock.caption: A world clock displays the current time in several places at once, one clock face per time zone.

writing-sprint-timer.alt: A pencil resting on an open book, trailing a springy coiled line toward a small circular loading icon
writing-sprint-timer.caption: A writing sprint sets a fixed block of time to get words down without pausing to edit.

yoga-session-timer.alt: A person in a lunging yoga pose with arms extended, framed by plants and a large dial behind them
yoga-session-timer.caption: A yoga timer can mark how long to hold each pose and how long the overall session runs.

yoga-timer.alt: A person folded forward in a downward-facing pose on a rolled mat, with a lit candle nearby and a large stopwatch behind them
yoga-timer.caption: A simple stopwatch running in the background is often all a yoga session needs to keep poses and pacing consistent.

iganony.alt: A story circle emptying like an hourglass beside a relay server that passes a request on to a padlocked private profile it cannot open
iganony.caption: An anonymous viewer hides you from the person who posted — not from Instagram, and not from whoever runs the viewer. The 24-hour clock is why the category exists at all.

picuki.alt: A signpost reading Picuki with one weathered arm pointing at a closed door and three newer arms pointing to separate unrelated buildings
picuki.caption: One name, several destinations. The original address stopped serving an Instagram viewer, and unrelated operators picked the name up — which is the real lesson about tools like this.
